title: Only 7% Pass This Nursing Entrance Exam
summary: Anatomy, vital signs, safety, numeracy and patient-care judgement combine in one focused entrance challenge.

landing.intro: Think you have the knowledge, calm judgement and people skills to make it through the challenge?

about.body:
This Clinical Admissions Lab condenses entrance-level nursing knowledge into one varied ten-question challenge. It covers anatomy and physiology, healthcare numeracy, observation trends, infection prevention, patient communication and calm prioritisation.

The challenge is designed for curious adults, prospective nursing students and healthcare learners around the world. It uses universal principles such as noticing deterioration, protecting dignity, reducing infection risk, communicating clearly and seeking appropriate qualified help—never country-specific policies or specialist treatment decisions.

Your final percentage reflects only the answers given in this entertainment quiz. It is a playful snapshot of the entrance areas that felt strongest and the topics that proved more challenging, not a judgement of clinical competence or suitability for nursing.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Complete ten varied admissions questions and choose the single answer best supported by the visible information.
Correct answers stay hidden while you play, so inspect every sequence, observation board and patient-care clue carefully.
Finish the assessment to reveal your Nursing Score, strongest entrance area and complete result report.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited nursing entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Healthcare procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local policy and qualified clinical guidance.

profiles.title: The Admissions Standout
profiles.copy: You combined strong foundational knowledge with calm, careful judgement across the entire admissions lab. Details, trends and patient-centred decisions stayed clear even when the cases became more demanding.

profiles.title: The Nursing Natural
profiles.copy: You showed an excellent feel for the knowledge and judgement behind safe, compassionate care. Most of the lab’s numerical, observational and communication traps did not pull you off course.

profiles.title: The Calm Candidate
profiles.copy: You handled a broad mix of body knowledge, safety decisions and patient scenarios with steady reasoning. A few finer details kept the entrance challenge interesting.

profiles.title: The Careful Problem-Solver
profiles.copy: You built a solid result by following the evidence and treating patient safety seriously. Your strongest stage shows where your clinical-learning instincts are already taking shape.

profiles.title: The Promising Applicant
profiles.copy: You solved a good share of the admissions lab and showed useful instincts across several care areas. The answer review will reveal which concepts are ready for another look.

profiles.title: The Compassionate Explorer
profiles.copy: The lab uncovered some knowledge gaps, but it also found moments of thoughtful, patient-centred judgement. Every explanation is a fresh chance to strengthen the foundations behind safe care.

insights.overview: Your nursing score at a glance

details.analysisTitle: How to read your nursing score
details.analysisCopy: This ten-question result combines body knowledge, healthcare numeracy, observation trends, infection prevention, communication and calm prioritisation. Each answer moves the percentage by ten points, so the grouped skill pattern below provides important context for the headline score.
details.roadmapIntro: Your score is only the first signal. Continue through the report to see which entrance areas held strongest and how your judgement changed across different care scenarios.
details.positionCopy: The entertainment challenge target is eight correct answers out of ten. Your marker shows how close this attempt came without assessing clinical competence.
details.measuredIntro: The selected questions span three broad parts of entrance-level nursing thinking without teaching diagnosis or treatment.

measuredAreas.title: Clinical foundations
measuredAreas.copy: Following basic physiology and solving simple time, rate and measurement questions.

measuredAreas.title: Observation and priorities
measuredAreas.copy: Noticing meaningful change and using several visible clues to decide what matters first.

measuredAreas.title: Safety and communication
measuredAreas.copy: Reducing infection risk while protecting privacy, dignity and understanding.

details.tipsTitle: Three ways to sharpen clinical reasoning
details.tipsIntro: These are general quiz strategies—not clinical instruction, medical advice or a professional assessment.

tips.title: Compare with the baseline
tips.copy: A new change from the earlier condition can matter more than one isolated measurement.

tips.title: Look for immediate danger
tips.copy: Airway, breathing, circulation and sudden changes in consciousness take priority over routine comfort needs.

tips.title: Choose the concrete response
tips.copy: In communication questions, prefer the option that listens, protects dignity or checks understanding.

details.finalCopy: You finished with {score} correct answers out of {total}. Your candidate profile for this attempt is shown below.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.explanation: The heart contracts to move blood through the circulation.

questions.question: How much time passes from 09:20 to 10:05?
questions.explanation: There are 40 minutes to 10:00, then 5 more minutes to 10:05: 45 minutes total.

questions.question: A task may splash body fluid towards the face. Which protection addresses that stated risk?
answers: No protection if the task is brief
questions.explanation: Eye or face protection is selected when the risk assessment identifies possible splashes to the face.

questions.question: Someone asks a sensitive question in a busy public area. What should you do?
answers: Answer loudly so everyone can hear
Discuss the details with nearby visitors
Offer to continue the conversation somewhere private
questions.explanation: Moving the conversation to a private setting protects confidentiality and dignity.

questions.question: Which measurement changed?

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse unchanged, breathing increased, temperature unchanged and alertness unchanged

questions.explanation: Breathing changed from 16 to 24 while the other recorded observations stayed the same.

questions.question: Which route correctly follows oxygen into the circulation?
questions.explanation: Oxygen travels through the airway to the lungs, then crosses into the blood.

questions.question: You count 9 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the rate per minute?
questions.explanation: Thirty seconds is half a minute, so doubling 9 gives 18 breaths per minute.

questions.question: Who has priority?
questions.explanation: New breathing difficulty that limits speech signals an immediate airway or breathing concern.

items: PERSON B::Breathing difficulty · cannot finish sentence
visual.ariaLabel: Person A is comfortable and asks for a blanket. Person B has breathing difficulty and cannot finish a sentence.

questions.question: What is the safest conclusion?
answers: There is clear deterioration requiring prompt qualified assessment
The trend is reassuring because no exact diagnosis is given
Wait for another shift before reporting it
questions.explanation: New confusion, pallor and faster breathing together show major deterioration from the earlier condition.

visual.ariaLabel: Earlier alert with normal colour and comfortable breathing. Now confused, pale and breathing faster.

questions.question: Who has immediate priority?
answers: Person A, because discomfort always comes first
Person B, because consciousness and breathing have suddenly changed
Both can wait for a routine check
Choose based on who arrived first
questions.explanation: A sudden change in consciousness with irregular breathing signals immediate danger and needs urgent qualified help.

items: PERSON A::Alert · mild stable discomfort · normal speech
PERSON B::Pale · difficult to wake · irregular breathing
visual.ariaLabel: Person A is alert with mild stable discomfort and normal speech. Person B is pale, difficult to wake and breathing irregularly.
